tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Harnack's inequality, mean-value form]

↗ def:ball-mean-value-property ↗ thm:harnack-local-mvp

\group Harmonic Functions

Let $n\ge 1$, let $U\subset \R ^n$ be open, and let $V$ be connected and bounded with $\overline V\subset U$. There is $C>0$, depending only on $V$, such that \[ u(x)\le C u(y)\qquad (x,y\in V) \] for every nonnegative $u\in C(U)$ with the ball mean-value property.
Proof

↗ thm:harnack-local-mvp

\sketch Choose $r>0$ so every $B(z,2r)$, $z\in \overline V$, lies in $U$, and cover $\overline V$ by finitely many $r/2$-balls. Connectivity makes the intersection graph of those meeting $V$ connected. Iterating the local bound along a path of at most $N$ balls yields $u(x)\le (2^n)^N u(y)$.

□
